docs.title: Feasibility Study of Short Time Aerobic Composting Using Vegetable Peels
docs.text: Type: B.Tech Project-II Final Thesis Report (CE-4291) Institution: Department of Civil Engineering, IIEST Shibpur Supervisors: Prof. Debabrata Mazumder, Prof. Chanchal Majumdar

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: This project investigates accelerated aerobic composting of vegetable peels using structural pit reactors, evaluating decomposition efficiency across a compressed 7 to 14 day timeline. Key parameters monitored include total organic carbon (via Chemical Oxygen Demand), nitrogen content (via Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen), temperature variation, and moisture balance, providing a basis for assessing the feasibility of rapid composting methods for organic waste management.

docs.title: Assessment of Water Quality in the Dry Season: A Case Study in the Little Feni River, Bangladesh
docs.text: Journal: IOSR Journal of Environmental Science, Toxicology and Food Technology Publication Date: June 2025 Author: Joyanta Debnath, Department of Civil Engineering, IIEST Shibpur

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
This study evaluates water quality during the dry season across seven sampling locations along the Musapur Reservoir. Results indicate elevated salinity levels, ranging from 1.5 to 8.03 parts per thousand, along with measurable concentrations of heavy metals including lead and cadmium, reflecting seasonal brackish water intrusion. These findings suggest that while the water may not be immediately suitable for domestic use without targeted filtration, it remains within acceptable thresholds for irrigation and supports the local fisheries sector.

docs.title: Varuna: A Python-Based System for Water Quality Index Calculation
docs.text: Journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology Publication Date: May 2025 Authors: Joyanta Debnath (IIEST Shibpur), Ananta Debnath (BUET)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Varuna is a Python-based software system developed to automate water resource quality assessments. The system implements multiple standardized indices, including the traditional Water Quality Index (WQI), the Canadian Water Quality Index (CWQI), and the NSF Water Quality Index. Built using the Pandas and Matplotlib libraries, Varuna processes large, multivariate water quality datasets and generates concise, tabular summaries suitable for engineering and environmental reporting.
